title: Imaging ML with group-aware evidence and recovery.
summary: A twelve-label MRI project with scanner-grouped evidence, ordered context, validated data and numerical contracts, and recoverable training. Public controls are fitted on authored data and clearly separated from the private model.
scope: The Python check verifies public source, retained notebook evidence, and research contracts. Optional Node tests execute the synthetic browser training pipeline. Historical MRI evaluation is separate; no clinical validity is established by these demonstrations.
private_boundary: MRI/DICOM images, patient or study identifiers, private prediction rows, trained weights, exact tuned inference recipes, and private GPU checkpoints remain excluded.

cards.title: Respect acquisition groups during validation.
cards.decision: Keep scanner groups disjoint and inspect aligned targets rather than relying on a random row split.
cards.boundary: Grouped development measurements are not evidence of clinical deployment readiness.

cards.title: Preserve global pooling across microbatches.
cards.decision: Normalize attention over all encoded windows; independent chunk softmax is not equivalent.
cards.boundary: These are numerical reference contracts, not the private MRI model recipe.

cards.title: Make fold recovery content-bound.
cards.decision: Demonstrate checkpoint verification, corruption rejection, and completed-fold reuse in a small public pipeline.
cards.boundary: The synthetic tabular pipeline demonstrates engineering behavior, not MRI diagnosis.

cards.title: Keep score scope and inference validity separate.
cards.decision: Validate twelve-label metrics, row ordering, and uncertainty decisions without treating an integration fixture as clinical evidence.
cards.boundary: A schema-valid prediction file does not establish an accurate or deployable model.

cards.title: Evaluate probabilities against a held-out baseline.
cards.decision: Compare per-label Brier and log loss, training-fold prevalence and scanner slices alongside AUC; preserve reliability-bin counts.
cards.boundary: Synthetic diagnostics do not establish calibration or clinical performance on MRI.
